narrative.overview:
A designer's notebook left open in soft afternoon light. The page is warm paper with a fine film grain over everything; behind the homepage, large blurred fields of sage, dusty blue, butter and peach drift slowly like light moving across a desk. On top of that light sit frosted glass panes: cards, pills and chips that are soft to the eye and lift gently when touched. Type does the talking. Instrument Serif is set huge and always at weight 400, with italics carrying the emphasis, and every fact is filed under a small JetBrains Mono caption in spaced capitals, like a label on a specimen jar.

The system has two registers. The **homepage** is the sunlit desk: glows, glass, ASCII flowers, bubbles that drift with scroll and shy away from the cursor, thumbnails that start soft-focus and sharpen when you look at them. The **case studies** are the notebook's written pages lit by the same window: drifting colour behind the header and the end of the page, softer light along the margins, an ASCII lily beside the title and an ASCII flower meadow before "Next up", while the reading column itself stays on calm paper with quiet translucent surfaces, generous measure and an inverted ink panel for reflections. The **About page** is lit the same way: colour behind the header and the end of the page, the lily peeking out from behind the portrait, and the meadow above the footer. Both registers work in light and dark; dark mode is a deep green-black night with cream ink, not a grey inversion.

Craft lives in small, rewarded details: a sheen that slides across a card on hover, colour swatches in a card's footer, a drop cap, butter-highlighter emphasis in prose, hand-made ASCII critters in place of missing thumbnails.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and green-black ink, with a global film grain layer.
A serif for headings and a modern sans for reading text, all at weight 400; hierarchy from size, italics and mono labels.
Pastel light fields (homepage only) under frosted glass.
Pills everywhere for actions and tags; generous rounded cards.
One text colour: all words are ink (or ink-soft for secondary text); emphasis is italic, never coloured.
Slow, soft motion on a shared easing curve; everything respects reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Text is never coloured for emphasis: headings, emphasised words, numbers and arrows all use the ink colour, with italics doing the emphasising. Pastels light the page; they never carry words.

rules.name: The Pastels-Are-Light Rule
rules.body: Sage, blue, butter, peach and coral appear as blurred light, gradients, highlighter and swatches. Never as flat solid UI fills behind body text.

rules.name: The Two-Theme Rule
rules.body: Every colour decision is made through the custom properties on `:root`, with a dark value defined for both the system-preference block and `[data-theme="dark"]`. No hard-coded colour may break dark mode (the white label backgrounds on thumbnails are the deliberate exception: they sit on fixed light artwork).

rules.name: The Heading Speaks Alone Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow, kicker, section number or tiny mono label above (or beside) a heading. If a fact matters, it goes in the meta table or the heading itself; if a block needs a title, it gets a real serif heading.

rules.name: The Single Weight Rule
rules.body: Everything is weight 400. Hierarchy comes from size, italics, ink vs ink-soft, and the switch between serif, sans and mono. Even `<strong>` stays 400 and gets a butter highlighter instead of bold.

rules.name: The Italic Voice Rule
rules.body: Italic is the emphasis voice: the second half of a heading, "Read case study", emphasised words in prose. It is the only emphasis; the colour never changes.

rules.name: The Margin Note Rule
rules.body: Facts (dates, codes, team size, role, tags) go in the mono label style, never in the serif.

rules.name: The Glass-Needs-Light Rule
rules.body: Glass only appears where there is coloured light behind it to frost (the homepage, and the case-study header). Where there is no light behind it, use the Quiet Surface instead.

rules.name: The Even Edge Rule
rules.body: Cards and surfaces have the same border on every side. No coloured strip along one edge (left rules, top bars) to signal a category.

rules.name: The Readable Fallback Rule
rules.body: Where `backdrop-filter` is unsupported, glass, pills and the theme toggle fall back to 92% paper so text stays legible.

dos: **Do** keep every heading and body text at weight 400; create emphasis with italics, size or the butter highlighter, never with a text colour.
**Do** put all facts, dates, tags and codes in the 11px mono label style with 0.12em tracking.
**Do** define every colour as a `:root` custom property with values for both light and dark themes.
**Do** use pills (999px) for actions and tags, and glass only over coloured light.
**Do** use the shared soft easing (`cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`) for lifts, sheens and focus effects, and disable animation and transitions under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** keep reading pages calm: 820px column, 21px prose at 62ch, Quiet Surface blocks, hairline section dividers.
**Do** give any image that starts soft-focus a sharp state on hover, focus and touch devices.
**Do** punctuate with commas, colons, semicolons, parentheses or full stops; use "·" as the separator in page titles.
donts: **Don't** put glow fields or drifting light on the About page, or strong light directly under case-study prose: on case studies keep the middle glows in the margins.
**Don't** drift toward a corporate SaaS look: no sharp-cornered saturated blue buttons, stock icon sets, or generic dashboard styling.
**Don't** colour any text: no terracotta, pastel or coral words; ASCII art is the only coloured lettering.
**Don't** add typefaces beyond the three: Instrument Serif (headings), Instrument Sans (reading text), JetBrains Mono (labels).
**Don't** put tiny subheadings (eyebrows, kickers, numbered section marks like "01 The problem", counters like "(01 / 06)") above or beside headings.
**Don't** use em dashes anywhere: copy, titles, citations or labels.
**Don't** give cards or callouts a single coloured strip (a thick left border or top bar); keep borders even.
